title: Copilot review request workflow: publish the draft and request the review as steps of one job, gated to Copilot bot PRs
answers: Why does the Copilot review workflow mark a draft PR ready for review itself?
Why are gh pr ready and the Copilot review request in the same job instead of two jobs?
Where is the logic that publishes Copilot draft PRs and requests @copilot review?
Why does a maintainer's draft PR never get auto-published?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/copilot-review.yml:request-review handles pull_request_target opened, ready_for_review and review_requested events. It requests a Copilot review for non-draft PRs from OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR authors or from the Copilot bot, and for Copilot-bot draft PRs on review_requested it runs the 'Mark ready for review' step (gh pr ready) before the 'Request Copilot review' step (gh pr edit --add-reviewer @copilot).
Rule: keep the publish step and the review-request step in the same job so they run in one invocation. A write made with GITHUB_TOKEN (gh pr ready) does not start other workflow runs, so a separate job would publish the PR and never receive the ready_for_review event it needs. Gate the draft path on github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'Copilot' and user.type == 'Bot' so maintainer drafts are never published automatically.
Symptom: Copilot PRs are created as drafts and the earlier trigger set (opened, ready_for_review) missed the review-request trigger, so Copilot PRs were never reviewed.
Constraints: the draft path runs only for review_requested on a draft Copilot bot PR; non-draft paths keep the OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR or Copilot-bot author condition. The job's permissions are pull-requests: write only. The PR description says markPullRequestReadyForReview may need contents: write (cli/cli#8910), and a review comment reports 'Resource not accessible by integration' without it and asks for contents: write to be granted now. The diff does not add it, so check the first run of the publish step before assuming it works.
applies: Edits to .github/workflows/copilot-review.yml trigger types or the Mark ready / Request review steps; for any workflow where one step's side effect must start a later workflow, prefer same-job sequencing over a separate job.
says: Why did requesting review on a bot draft pull request fail to start the review?
Human maintainer draft pull requests should never be automatically published when requesting reviews.
Automated code reviews never arrived on draft pull requests opened by the coding bot.
Automatically publish bot draft pull requests and request review in a single unified step.
Prevent developer draft pull requests from being published when automated reviewers are assigned.
search: In .github/workflows/copilot-review.yml:request-review, publishing a draft PR with gh pr ready and requesting a Copilot review with gh pr edit --add-reviewer @copilot are combined within a single job. Running both steps sequentially in one job prevents missed events, as actions taken with GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger downstream workflows. Draft publishing is gated to pull requests where user.login == 'Copilot' and user.type == 'Bot', preventing maintainer drafts from being published automatically. The job specifies pull-requests: write permissions, with a known potential need for contents: write.
